title: Observation: the envelope of every fact the tool shows
description: Every module output that reaches a page, the JSON API or a CLI --json stream is one of these. The envelope carries where the fact came from (sources: the exact command or API call) and when (observed_at), so each page can show data age and link each fact to its command. Set kinds (produced as a complete set per scope: pin_state, host_compare, containment, silicon_protection, mirror_status, repo_inventory, runner_settings, credential_status, registry_record) carry a `snapshot`; their current value is the latest COMPLETE snapshot of the scope, so a fact that is no longer produced disappears. Event kinds (rewrite_alert, t0_result, alert) keep the latest observation per `subject`. The SQLite database stores these and can be rebuilt from mirrors, registry and CI (except the runs and actions tables). Owner: each producing module; storage by db. A3, H1, H6.

subject.description: <kind>:<key>, starting with this document's kind. Keys per kind are listed in docs/contracts/README.md.

observed_at.description: A3: the OLDEST observation time of any input, so the envelope never looks fresher than its data. Not expressible in JSON Schema; db.put enforces it (interfaces.md section 12).

snapshot.description: Required for set kinds (see the top-level description and README section 4). db.put refuses a set-kind observation without one.

release_check.description: Wave B releases (CR-R1): one check of a release draft or of its re-verification. `verdict` uses README section 6 gate verdicts (NOT-RUN with a reason never blocks); `person` marks a step only a person can complete (a tag, an approval, a tier with no runner here): the draft lists it, never does it.

release_draft.description: Wave B releases (CR-R1; G2, G3, G4, G7, F4): one LOCAL release draft of a registered configuration, written as a folder (release lock or draft lock, ERRATA.md and .html, release notes, the person-only checklist, the unsigned gate ledger, the generated-RTL md5 manifest). Nothing is tagged, pushed or published: `published` is always false and every tag or approval is a person step. `verdict` is the README section 6 run ladder over the checks (FAIL > UNVERIFIED > INFRA > WAIVED > WARN > PASS; NOT-RUN ignored). `ready` = the lock is complete and every check the tool makes (`person` false) is PASS, WARN, WAIVED or NOT-RUN; the person checks (UNVERIFIED until a person acts) and steps remain, so a ready draft's verdict may still be UNVERIFIED, never FAIL or INFRA. Event kind (`release_draft:<configuration>:<version>`). Additive optional $defs: no schema bump.

kind.description: G2: fix needs T0-T3, feature adds T4, tapeout adds T6.

errata.description: F4: the document revision is the highest doc_revision of the configuration's records (1 with none); `digest` is the md5 of the rendered entries (ERRATA.md below its header), so it changes exactly when a record's rendered text does.

archive.description: G7: the generated-RTL archive and its md5 manifest, or null when none was given.

train.description: G4: members of the release train, deepest first (the order they are finalised): components in the tree whose pinned commit carries no release tag.

release_verify.description: Wave B releases (CR-R1): `nanosoc-rm release verify DIR` re-checks a draft against the mirrors and the registry now: the release commit and every lock pin still resolve with the same state, the release and keep tags still point where the draft saw them, the archive still matches its manifest, the errata document re-renders to the same digest, and every file still has the md5 draft.json recorded. `drift` lists each difference. Event kind (`release_verify:<configuration>:<version>`). Additive optional $defs.

fork_status.description: Wave B releases (CR-R1; I1, I2 read-only part): one fork of an example project, found through the host's fork API read anonymously (GET only). `ahead`/`behind` against the upstream default branch; `based_on` is the newest upstream tag the merge base contains; `releases_behind` the upstream release tags (vX.Y.Z) after it. `user_paths` is judged only when the upstream declares a fork contract (component-manifest `fork_contract`, I2): otherwise NOT-RUN with the reason. Never writes to a fork. Event kind (`fork_status:<component>:<host>:<fork path>`). Additive optional $defs.

contract.description: I2: whether the upstream at its default branch declares a fork contract and documents the upgrade steps.

verdict.description: PASS up to date; WARN behind or diverged; UNVERIFIED could not read the fork.

compat_result.description: CR-11 (MVP S2, `nanosoc-rm compat`, interfaces.md section 9a): one LOCAL compatibility check of a configuration's tree, optionally with pin overrides (`--pin TREE_PATH=SHA`). The tree is resolved by the pin walker with each override replacing the gitlink at its tree path; the configuration T0 gates then run locally (run mode `local`: anonymous, outside CI) with their negative controls, and roll up by README section 6 with the configuration's t0_waivers. `t0.runner.hardened` is always NOT-RUN with detail `local run` in this mode: never PASS, never FAIL. With overrides, `t0.clone.upgrade-path` may also be NOT-RUN (it clones the registered commit). `unjudged_overrides`: overrides the gates' anonymous walk did not reach; any makes the verdict UNVERIFIED. Event kind (`compat_result:<configuration>:<nonce>`), stored only on request and only for a run without overrides (a what-if is not a fact). Additive optional $defs (README section 2 rule 4): no schema bump.

commit.description: The configuration's root commit the tree was resolved from.

pins.description: One per pin of the (overridden) tree, as the walker lists them: first tree path, every tree path, the walker's facts, and each configuration gate's item result at the pin's tree path (absent when the gate judged no item there).

state.description: B3 state on the pinned host (or the pin-level LOCAL_URL / NO_GITLINK); null when unjudged (an unknown URL).

split.description: B7: the pin's component is pinned at more than one commit in this tree.

splits.description: B7: each component pinned at more than one commit in this tree, with its pins.

reason.description: Why the verdict is UNVERIFIED beyond the gates (an override the gates did not reach).

over_budget.description: D1: longer than the T0 budget (120 s). A warning; never changes the verdict.

work_dir.description: The kept work directory (--keep-work), else null.

run_verdict.description: CR-12: present exactly when `tier` is. The run verdict ladder (README section 6: FAIL > UNVERIFIED > INFRA > WAIVED > WARN > PASS) over the T0 roll-up `verdict` and the tier's verdict; a tier skipped because T0 is FAIL (NOT-RUN) leaves FAIL. The exit code follows it. `verdict` stays the T0 roll-up alone.

compat_tier.description: CR-12 (MVP S3, `nanosoc-rm compat --tier t1|t2`, interfaces.md section 9a 'Tiers'): one local T1 or T2 run of the registry's tiers.yaml command for the configuration, in a sandbox checkout of the resolved (overridden) tree. `rows` are verdicts.tsv rows (result-bundle verdict_row, this run's nonce): always `tier.<tier>` from the exit code (FAIL on a nonzero exit or a kill), plus `tier.<tier>.<gate>` for each row of the declared verdicts file. A run killed at 1.5 x budget is FAIL. Over budget is a warning (`over_budget`). NOT-RUN only when T0 is FAIL and nobody forced the tier. `forced`: a person ran the tier past a T0 FAIL with --force-tier; the result is UNVERIFIED for release whatever the tier says. Additive optional $defs: no schema bump.

reason.description: Why the tier is not PASS (or why it did not run); on a PASS, null unless forced (then the --force-tier note).

command.description: The command as declared (an argv list joined shell-quoted).

env_keys.description: The names of the explicit env entries (values are not recorded: they may name licence servers).

timeout_s.description: The hard kill limit: budget_s x 1.5.

seconds.description: Wall time of the command; null when it never started.

missing_paths.description: Tree paths of needed pins the sandbox checkout could not lay out (no anonymous fetch reached the commit); any makes the tier UNVERIFIED without running.

not_laid_out.description: Pins of the tree left out of the sandbox because the tiers.yaml `pins` list does not need them.

log_tail.description: The last lines of the command's combined output.

branch_state.description: CR8 (MVP S1, `nanosoc-rm branches`): one branch of one repo, judged from the local mirror only. Set kind: one snapshot per repo (`branch_state:<host>:<path>`), so a deleted branch disappears from the current view. `ahead`/`behind` are rev-list counts against the repo's default branch; `merged` = the tip is an ancestor of the default branch; `tags` are the tags whose tip IS this tip (`keep_tags` the keep/* subset); `pins` are registered pins (any pin of any stored walk, section 4) whose commit the tip reaches and the default branch does not; `cited` the registry's structured citations (defect benches, fixes) likewise reached. Verdict, first match: MERGED, PROTECTED (a tag on the tip), PINNED (a pin or citation reaches into it), STALE (last commit older than `stale_days`), ACTIVE. `deletable` = MERGED or STALE with no pin, no citation and no tag; the tool prints the command for a person and never runs it. Additive optional $defs (README section 2 rule 4): no schema bump.

ahead.description: Commits on the branch that the default branch lacks.

behind.description: Commits on the default branch that the branch lacks.

branch_head.description: One side of a host compare. `default_branch` and `head` are null only when that side could not be read (relation UNKNOWN).

host_compare.description: B6: a component's canonical default branch against one copy's. Counts come from rev-list in ONE object store holding both hosts' refs, never from one host's API alone (which cannot see the other host's commits). SAME = 0/0; AHEAD = the canonical has commits the copy lacks and the copy has none of its own; BEHIND = the reverse; DIVERGED = both sides have their own; UNRELATED = no merge base (counts null); UNKNOWN = a side could not be read (its latest mirror_status is not ok, or its default-branch ref is absent from the mirror); counts null, and an unreadable side's head may be null. `default_branch_mismatch` = the two default branches have different names (ASIC-Flow: GitHub lpddr4-pll, GitLab main), so the comparison is between differently named branches.

containment.description: B4: does one configuration contain commit X of one component, on one host? Counts only commits reachable from that host's branches and tags. `no` requires every pin decided false; an undecided pin (contains null) makes the answer `unknown`, never `no`. One row per (configuration, host where the component has a repo), `absent` included (interfaces.md section 6).

answer.description: yes = every pin of the component contains X; partial = some do (a split tree, B7); no = none do; absent = the component is not in this tree; unknown = at least one pin could not be decided.

reason.description: Required when contains is null: which commit could not be proven to exist on this host.

silicon_protection.description: B5: one commit in a silicon or frozen tree that its component's default branch cannot reach, judged on ONE host. Rows are emitted for the host the pin's URL names (`pinned`: what a recursive clone uses) and for the component's canonical host (`canonical`: where C10 protective tags belong); one row when they are the same host. `state` is the B3 state of the commit on that host. `covered` = a tag on that host contains the commit (judged by containment, not by tag name).

pinned.description: This row's host is the one the pinned URL names.

canonical.description: This row's host is the component's canonical host.

state.description: B3 state on this host. Never ON_DEFAULT: a commit the default branch reaches is not a protection row.

rewrite_alert.description: B8: a default branch moved to a commit that does not descend from its previous head (a force-push). Keyed on the branch NAME: a change of which branch is the default is not a rewrite.

lost_commits.description: Commits reachable from old_head and from no current branch or tag on this host.

pinned_lost.description: Registered pins whose commit is among the lost ones.

mirror_status.description: H6: one mirror fetch. The page shows now - last_success_at as the mirror's age.

access.description: CR-PR1: how the repo was read. anonymous = no credential; credentials = private, readable with the host's private_read method; unreadable = the fetch failed (see cause). Absent on rows stored before CR-PR1.

cause.description: CR-PR1: why a fetch failed, from git's error text (auth, ssh-key, ssh-host, not-found, network, timeout, config = private_read unusable, other); null when ok.

method.description: CR-PR1: the private_read method this sync tried (ssh or token), null when only the anonymous fetch ran. Never the credential itself.

repo_inventory.description: A1: one repo found by listing the GitHub org and the GitLab group (with subgroups). `unclassified` = in no catalogue entry, and is flagged. `ignored` = listed in the catalogue's `ignored` section with a reason (a repo in the org that is not nanoSoC-related): classified, not tracked, not flagged.

t0_result.description: One T0 run as the service sees it: from trigger (pending) to an accepted, rejected (D5) or refused (D11) bundle, or no bundle at all. A2: every run records who or what started it. The run verdict follows README section 6: FAIL if any gate FAILs; else UNVERIFIED if any gate is UNVERIFIED or no gate PASSed (nothing was checked); else INFRA if any gate is INFRA; else WAIVED if any gate is WAIVED (a frozen configuration's known failures, GATE2 Q1); else WARN if any gate is WARN (CR-9: passed with listed warnings, amber); else PASS. A WARN gate counts as checked.

triggered_by.description: A2, H2: the GitHub login that pressed Run, or `schedule`.

acceptance.description: pending: triggered, not fetched. accepted: bundle verified (D5) and scanned clean (D11). rejected: verification failed (D5). refused: the vendor scan found something or could not run (D11); the bundle is not stored. no-bundle: the job ended without a bundle; INFRA when the CI API gives an infrastructure cause (D7), else UNVERIFIED.

reason.description: Why a bundle was rejected or refused, or why the run is INFRA.

verdict.description: README section 6: FAIL > UNVERIFIED > INFRA > WAIVED > WARN > PASS (CR-9), and PASS, WARN or WAIVED needs at least one PASS or WARN gate (all gates NOT-RUN or WAIVED is UNVERIFIED). WARN: no gate FAIL, UNVERIFIED, INFRA or WAIVED, at least one gate WARN. WAIVED: no gate FAIL, UNVERIFIED or INFRA, at least one gate WAIVED by the configuration's t0_waivers. NOT-RUN gates are counted and shown beside the verdict. null while pending. A rejected or refused bundle gives UNVERIFIED.

control.description: D6: fired / not-fired / missing, or not-applicable for a NOT-RUN gate (nothing ran, so there is no control to fire). A PASS gate whose control did not fire, or is missing, is UNVERIFIED.

raw_verdict.description: Present only on a WAIVED gate: the verdict before waivers (README section 6 table), FAIL or UNVERIFIED. The waiver never erases it.

waived.description: Present only on a WAIVED gate: every non-pass item and the waiver that covers it (`covered_by` = the waiver's tree_path; differs from `tree_path` for a not-reached item below a waived one).

started_at.description: D1: from the D5-verified bundle's provenance. null until accepted.

finished_at.description: D1: from the D5-verified bundle's provenance. null until accepted.

over_budget.description: D1: finished_at - started_at exceeded the tier's budget (T0: 120 s). A warning shown beside the verdict; it never changes the verdict. The job's 15-minute timeout is the kill limit, not the budget.

runner.description: D10: the runner that ran the job, from the CI API's job record (never from the bundle). Verify rejects a runner id outside ci.allowed_runner_ids.

runner_settings.description: D10, H1: the CI runner's settings as the runner API reports them, compared with the expected hardened values. Shown as the dashboard's runner status. `readable: false` = the poller's token could not read the runner (settings null, verdict unverified).

expected.description: The hardened values from the private config (interfaces.md section 1, ci.runner_expected).

drift.description: One entry per setting that differs from `expected`, e.g. `run_untagged: true, expected false`.

credential_status.description: H3: one service credential, its scope as recorded in the private config, its scope as the host reports it (where the host can say), and its expiry. A credential that could not be checked is `unverified` with a reason, never `ok`. No token value ever appears here.

project.description: The CI project a trigger token is recorded against (A2).

registry_record.description: A3, H1: one registry record (configuration, component, defect, erratum, import source) shown as a fact. observed_at = when the service last read the registry at `commit`; the source is `git -C <registry> show <commit>:<file>`.

pointer.description: JSON pointer of the record inside `file`; empty for a whole-file record.

record.description: The record exactly as the registry holds it (its own schema validates it).

alert.description: An alert the dashboard shows until someone clears it. Mirrors a row of the alerts table (interfaces.md section 12). `about` is the subject of the observation that raised it.

quality_density.description: CR-14 (Q1): comment density of one repository snapshot: per file, directory (2 levels), language and repository; ratio = (comment + docstring) / (code + comment + docstring); outliers exceed the language's max_ratio with at least min_lines non-blank lines. Markdown is counted separately in `docs`. Event kind, subject `quality_density:<target>:<commit>` (`<commit>+worktree` for a work-tree read, `worktree` without git), so stored results form a trend per target (Q5). Additive optional $defs (README section 2 rule 4): no schema bump.

target.description: A catalogue component id, a [quality] paths name, or the label of a --path run.

commit.description: The analysed commit; null for a directory that is not a git work tree.

worktree.description: true: read from a local directory as it is on disk (may differ from commit).

worktree_state.description: Work-tree reads only: a digest of the listed files' paths, modes, sizes and mtimes when read. A stored result whose digest differs from the disk is stale (the GUI re-analyses).

quality_finding.description: CR-14 (Q2): comment problems of one repository snapshot, each with file, line, evidence and a suggested edit; `edit` (whole-line replacement) is set where the change is mechanical and is what the patch applies. Event kind, subject `quality_finding:<target>:<commit>` (`<commit>+worktree` for a work-tree read, `worktree` without git), so stored results form a trend per target (Q5). Additive optional $defs (README section 2 rule 4): no schema bump.

readme_check.description: CR-14 (Q3): every path, make target, script, command, submodule, flow (make target -> recipe -> script) and layout entry each README names, checked against the tree at the commit; `mismatches` are the checks with status missing, `unverified` those the reader could not confirm (an unresolved Makefile include); `layout` is the generated Repository layout section. Event kind, subject `readme_check:<target>:<commit>` (`<commit>+worktree` for a work-tree read, `worktree` without git), so stored results form a trend per target (Q5). Additive optional $defs (README section 2 rule 4): no schema bump.

doc_score.description: CR-14 (Q4): conciseness of each Markdown file and section (words, sentence length, filler and hedge words, passive share, repeated sentences, paragraphs duplicated across files) and a 0-100 score, higher is more concise; `score` is the word-weighted mean; files are ranked worst first. Event kind, subject `doc_score:<target>:<commit>` (`<commit>+worktree` for a work-tree read, `worktree` without git), so stored results form a trend per target (Q5). Additive optional $defs (README section 2 rule 4): no schema bump.
